name: Gamma Absorption Kernel
formula:
h_i(tau) = w_i * Gamma(tau; k1, lambda1)
           + (1 - w_i) * Gamma(tau; k2, lambda2)

log Gamma = k*ln(lambda) + (k-1)*ln(t) - lambda*t - lgamma(k)
inputs:
dose_i (mg)
t_meal
meal type (solid / liquid / mixed)
outputs:
h_i(t):
absorption kernel
per nutrient i

name: Mass-Conserving Multi-Meal Absorption
formula:
Mass-conserving multi-meal absorption:
a_i(t) = SUM_m q_{i,m} * F_abs,i,m * h_i*(t - t_m)

h_i*(tau | t_m) = h_i(tau) * m_i(t_m + tau) /
                   INTEGRAL_0^inf h_i(s) * m_i(t_m + s) ds

Because INTEGRAL h_i* d tau = 1:
INTEGRAL a_i(t) dt = SUM_m q_{i,m} * F_abs,i,m <= SUM_m q_{i,m}.

Extent (F_abs) and timing (h_i*) are separated. Circadian, activity,
gastric-emptying, sleep and matrix effects may reshape timing but cannot create mass.
inputs: Gamma kernel h_i; bounded F_abs; positive normalized timing modulator m_i; meal events (q,t)
outputs: a_i(t): absorbed mass rate; integral exactly equals dose*F_abs

name: Positive Timing Modulator
formula:
Positive timing modulator:
m_i(t) = exp[
  eta_c1,i*cos(2*pi*(t-phi_1,i)/1440)
+ eta_c2,i*cos(4*pi*(t-phi_2,i)/1440)
+ eta_act,i*g_act(t)
+ eta_GE,i*g_GE(t)
+ eta_sleep,i*I_sleep(t)
+ eta_matrix,i(t)
]

m_i(t) > 0 by construction. It is normalized inside h_i*, so it changes
the absorption-time profile, not total absorbed mass.
inputs: Clock phase; activity; sleep; gastric emptying; matrix context
outputs: m_i(t)>0 used only inside normalized h_i*

name: Bounded Absorbed Fraction
formula:
Bounded absorbed fraction:
F_abs,i,m = F_max,i * sigmoid[
  logit(F_base,i / F_max,i)
- log1p(q_i,m / K_m,i)
+ SUM_j gamma_ij * tanh(z_j)
+ gamma_cook,i
+ gamma_condition,i
]

0 <= F_abs,i,m <= F_max,i <= 1.
All interaction/cooking terms act on the logit scale; the range is enforced
mathematically rather than only documented.
inputs: F_base,F_max,dose,Km,cooking,condition and interaction features

name: Gastric Emptying  (Weibull)
formula:
GE(t) = 1 - exp( -ln2 · (t / T_50)^kappa )

T_50:  60 - 120 min  (solid meals)
kappa: 0.5 - 2.0  [v39l F-I]
inputs:
Meal composition
Meal volume
Solid vs liquid

name: Activity / Sleep Timing Effect
formula:
Activity/sleep effect enters the positive timing modulator:
g_act(t) = MET(t) / (MET(t) + K_act)
m_act(t) = exp(beta_act * g_act(t) + beta_sleep * I_sleep(t))

The term is normalized through h_i*. If evidence supports a change in absorption
extent, include it as a bounded logit term inside F_abs, never as an unbounded multiplier.
inputs: MET, sleep state, K_act; optional evidence-tier extent modifier
outputs: Positive timing modifier or bounded logit extent term

name: Food-Matrix Guard
formula:
Food-matrix guard:
eta_matrix,i = SUM_j psi_ij * tanh(q_j / q_ref,j)

Phase 1: psi_ij = 0.
Future activation: eta_matrix enters logit(F_abs) or log m_i(t).
Do NOT use A_i * PRODUCT_j(1 + psi_ij*q_j/q_ref), because a negative factor
can reverse sign and a positive product can exceed the absorbed dose.
inputs: Co-food quantities; signed evidence-tier interaction coefficients
outputs: eta_matrix for A3/A4; no direct multiplicative mass factor

name: Elimination Rate Constant
formula:
k_el_i = ln(2) / T_half_i

T_half:  0.01 - 1000 days  (per nutrient)

(half-life in days)

name: Hepatic Clearance
formula:
*** CORRECTED v32.3 ***

CL_hepatic = Q_H * E_H

Well-stirred model. E_H already embeds protein binding:
  E_H = (f_u * CL_int) / (Q_H + f_u * CL_int)
Therefore f_u must NOT be multiplied again (it was double-counted in v32.2).

Q_H = 0.260 * CO   (ICRP Pub 89; age-dependent — Adult 0.260*CO; infants <2y ~0.10*CO rising to adult by 2-3y via O1 anthropometrics)
E_H = hepatic extraction ratio in [0,1]

Low-extraction limit (Q_H >> f_u*CL_int):  CL_hepatic ≈ f_u * CL_int
High-extraction limit (f_u*CL_int >> Q_H): CL_hepatic ≈ Q_H (flow-limited)

name: Dimensionless Cluster Exposure
formula:
Unit-invariant cluster exposure:
Cbar_i = w_i*C1_i + (1-w_i)*C2_i
sp_tau(z) = tau*log1p(exp(z/tau))

r_hi,i = max(0, sp_tau((ln(Cbar_i+eps)-ln(theta_hi,i+eps))/s_hi,i) - sp_tau(0))
r_lo,i = max(0, sp_tau((ln(theta_lo,i+eps)-ln(Cbar_i+eps))/s_lo,i) - sp_tau(0))

E_k(t) = SUM_i v_ik * (r_hi,i + r_lo,i)
v_ik >= 0; SUM_i v_ik = 1.

E_k is dimensionless and invariant to an upstream unit conversion when Cbar and
its thresholds are converted together. States retain typed physical units.
inputs: Typed C1/C2 states; same-unit thresholds; scales s_hi/s_lo; 80x12 weights

name: Exact Excess-Damage Integration
formula:
Exact excess-damage update for piecewise-constant forcing:
k_hi,k = ln(2) / T_half,hi,k
rho_hi,k = exp(-k_hi,k * dt_day)
g_hi,k = -expm1(-k_hi,k * dt_day) / k_hi,k
u_hi,k = eta_hi,k * max(E_k - theta_E,hi,k, 0)^p_hi,k

Z_hi,k(t+dt) = rho_hi,k*Z_hi,k(t) + g_hi,k*u_hi,k

Numerically stable limit: if |k_hi,k| < eps_k, set g_hi,k = dt_day.
inputs: E_k; dimensionless cluster threshold; eta,p; T_half; dt_day

name: Exact Deficiency-Damage Integration
formula:
Exact deficiency-damage update for piecewise-constant forcing:
k_lo,k = ln(2) / T_half,lo,k
rho_lo,k = exp(-k_lo,k * dt_day)
g_lo,k = -expm1(-k_lo,k * dt_day) / k_lo,k
u_lo,k = eta_lo,k * max(theta_E,lo,k - E_k, 0)^p_lo,k

Z_lo,k(t+dt) = rho_lo,k*Z_lo,k(t) + g_lo,k*u_lo,k

This preserves half-life compounding and removes time-step-dependent Euler forcing bias.
inputs: E_k; dimensionless cluster threshold; eta,p; T_half; dt_day

name: Total Damage + Activity
formula:
u_sed,k = eta_sed * softplus(SED - 480) * v_sed,k          [AU/day — a FORCING RATE]
Z_k(t+dt) = rho_k*Z_k(t) + g_k*(u_hi,k + u_lo,k + u_sed,k)
Activity modulation applies to the accumulated stock: Z_k <- Z_k * (1 - delta_k*MVPA/(MVPA + K_act))
inputs:
Z_hi, Z_lo
MVPA (min/wk)
SED (min/day sitting)
outputs:
Z_k:
net damage
modulated by activity
correction_applied: UNITS FIX. The sedentary term was a rate multiplied by dt and added to a stock outside the integrator, which made the result depend on step size. It is now a forcing term inside the exact zero-order-hold update, alongside the excess and deficiency forcings.

name: Dual-Hill Dose-Response
formula:
damage(C) = D_def * max(0, K_def^n1 - C^n1) / K_def^n1
           + D_tox * max(0, C^n2 - K_tox^n2) / (K_tox^n2 + C^n2)

U-shaped curve: both deficiency AND excess cause damage

name: Lab Fusion (single-entry via E)
formula:
Lab fusion - SINGLE ENTRY (no double-count):
Labs enter the estimator ONCE, via the Layer E innovation (E4): y_lab updates the posterior and its
uncertainty widens as the anchor ages. The displayed score derives from the FUSED state:
   D_final_k = D_k(fused state)
The separate re-blend  D_final = a*D_k + (1-a)*f(delta_clin)  is REMOVED (double-counted the same lab:
once in E, once here). Lab recency is surfaced as a data-quality flag ('last anchor: N days'), not a 2nd blend.

formula:
Composite wellness score - STABLE display (FIXED weights):

The adaptive weighting  w_k = base * max(D_final_k/50, 1)  is used ONLY for action PRIORITY in Layer H,
NEVER for the displayed composite (adaptive display weights make the score drift and break comparability).

name: Rao-Blackwellized Sigma Points
formula: PRIMARY FILTER: Rao-Blackwellized square-root UKF (RB-SR-UKF). Partition x=[x_L,x_N]: x_L in R^164 = 81 fast + 81 slow nutrient/exposure states + N2 extracellular volume + N5 autonomic tone; x_N in R^55 = damage/lifestyle/nonlinear mechanistic states. Nonlinear branches = 2*55+1 = 111. Full 219-state SR-UKF benchmark = 439 points. α=1.0, λ=0.
inputs: x_N(55), S_N; conditional linear block x_L(164)
outputs: 111 nonlinear sigma branches + exact conditional Gaussian linear block
correction_applied: ★v34.1 n=219 canonical; 111 nonlinear RB branches; 439 full SR-UKF benchmark; alpha=1.0

name: RB-SR-UKF Predict
formula:
RB-SR-UKF prediction:
For each nonlinear sigma branch j:
  x_N,j^- = f_N(x_N,j, u_t)
  m_L,j^- = A_j*m_L + B_j*u_t + b_j
  P_L,j^- = A_j*P_L*A_j^T + Q_L,j

A_j, B_j and Q_L,j are conditioned on branch-specific nonlinear modifiers.
Mix the 111 conditional Gaussian branches to obtain x_hat^-, S^- and P_LN^-.

Conditional-linearity gate:
If the PK block cannot be written linear-Gaussian after fixing x_N,j,
route that sub-block to the nonlinear partition or use the full 439-point SR-UKF benchmark.
inputs: 111 nonlinear branches; conditional A_j,B_j,Q_L,j; controls u_t

name: RB-SR-UKF Update, Gating & Smoothing
formula:
RB-SR-UKF measurement update:
1) Propagate each conditional branch through the nutrient-specific observation
   function y_hat_j = h(m_L,j^-, x_N,j^-).
2) Form innovation nu and S_y with square-root QR/cholupdate operations.
3) Gate with d^2 = nu^T*(S_y*S_y^T)^-1*nu.
4) Apply Student-t/Huber robust weighting to R or the innovation.
5) Perform conditional Kalman updates and recombine the 111 branches.

NO Kalman-gain floor. The primary covariance update remains square-root.
A Joseph form is permitted only as a documented fallback using an effective
statistical-linearization H_tilde.

Nightly enhancement: run a 7-14 day fixed-lag RB smoother for late logs/labs.
inputs: Measurements, nutrient-specific h_j, S_minus, R, robust gate
outputs: Posterior 219-state mean/covariance; observability class; smoothed recent states

name: Cause-Specific Hazard
formula:
*** CORRECTED ***

lambda_k(t | h_t) = softplus(W_k h_t + b_k), so lambda_k >= 0.

The vector contains independent positive intensities for declared wellness or outcome trajectories; it does not have to sum to one. Each output must declare one of three semantics: co-occurring multi-label, mutually exclusive first event, or multi-state transition. Consumer/clinician/partner rendering is a separate contract and must not change the underlying probability semantics.
inputs: h_t from F1
correction_applied:
*** P0-2:
was softmax / T
now softplus
(rates not probabilities)

name: Exact Multi-Outcome / Competing-Risk Update
formula:
Two valid trajectory semantics are supported.

A) DEFAULT - co-occurring wellness outcomes (multi-label):
  H_k,n+1 = H_k,n + lambda_k,n * dt
  F_k,n+1 = 1 - exp(-H_k,n+1)
Each outcome has its own cumulative hazard; no shared survival probability is imposed.

B) OPTIONAL - mutually exclusive first-event competing risks:
  Lambda_n = SUM_k lambda_k,n
  S_n+1 = S_n * exp(-Lambda_n*dt)
  DeltaF_k,n = S_n * (lambda_k,n/Lambda_n) * (1-exp(-Lambda_n*dt))
  use DeltaF_k,n=0 when Lambda_n=0.

For transitions after an event or coexisting conditions, use a multi-state transition
matrix/product-integral (Aalen-Johansen), not a single competing-risk survival product.
inputs: Positive hazard/intensity lambda_k and declared event semantics
outputs: Outcome-wise trajectory probabilities or exact competing-risk CIFs

name: Training Loss
formula:
L  =  L_NLL  +  alpha * L_ranking  +  beta * L_calibration

L_ranking:  concordance-based
L_calibration:  Brier score penalty

Training data

name: CATE Definition
formula:
tau(x)  =  E[ Y(1) - Y(0)  |  X = x ]

NOTE - Layer G has TWO build paths to the SAME Layer-H interface:
  INTERIM = static DR-learner (G1-G4) - BUILD FIRST (it is LTMLE's own scaffolding).   FULL = LTMLE (G5), upgrade later.
  See G4 and G5 for the what / why / how.
inputs: User features X

name: Cross-Fitted Outcomes
formula:
mu_hat_0(x),  mu_hat_1(x)
via K = 5 fold cross-fitting
Gradient boosting on historical data
★ Also the LTMLE nuisance stack (Super-Learner cross-fit): outcome Qbar_t=E[Y|Lbar_t,Abar_t], propensity g_t=P(A_t|Lbar_t,Abar_{t-1}) - feeds BOTH the DR-learner (G4) and LTMLE (G5).
inputs: Historical user data

name: DR Pseudo-Outcomes + Propensity
formula:
Y_tilde(1) = mu_hat_1 + W*(Y - mu_hat_1) / e_hat(X)
Y_tilde(0) = mu_hat_0 + (1-W)*(Y - mu_hat_0) / (1 - e_hat(X))

e_hat(X) = P(T=1|X)  clipped to [0.05, 0.95]
inputs:
mu_hat, e_hat
observed (W, Y, X)

name: DR-Learner CATE
formula:
tau_hat_DR(x)  =  Y_tilde(1)(x)  -  Y_tilde(0)(x)

============ BUILD PATH  -  G1-G4 = LTMLE's SCAFFOLDING - BUILD FIRST (serving it is a separate call) ============
WHAT  G1-G4 is the static DR-learner. It answers the SINGLE-DECISION question: given the user's
      current context X, what is the effect of an intervention vs not, right now? -> tau_hat_DR(x).
      Doubly-robust: consistent if EITHER the outcome model (mu_hat) OR the propensity (e_hat) is right.
WHY   Legitimate interim because (1) it needs only a CROSS-SECTIONAL cohort (one snapshot per user),
      not a longitudinal panel; (2) no backward-ICE / targeting sequence -> far lighter to build,
      store and run; (3) IF you later choose to serve it, Layer G can personalize before full LTMLE is ready
      (serving is OPTIONAL - see BUILD vs SERVE below). LIMIT: does NOT correct time-varying confounding (a covariate both
      changed by past intervention AND predicting future adherence). Fine for a single-decision
      recommendation; can bias the effect of a regime followed OVER TIME.
HOW   Fit cross-fitted mu_hat_0, mu_hat_1 (K=5) + propensity e_hat(X) clipped [0.05,0.95] (G2/G3);
      tau_hat_DR(x)=Ytilde(1)-Ytilde(0) (this row). Serve tau_hat_DR to H as the benefit prior.
      Runs OFFLINE batch, but LIGHT - NOT the heavy build that G5 is.

BUILD vs SERVE (do not conflate): the nuisance + cross-fitting + serving scaffolding is REQUIRED
      for LTMLE regardless -> BUILD it first (mandatory; it is a checkpoint on the LTMLE build).
      Whether to SERVE its cohort estimates now, or stay on priors until the panel supports LTMLE,
      is a SEPARATE, OPTIONAL decision.
inputs: Y_tilde from G3
units: INTERIM PATH - BUILD FIRST (it is LTMLE's own scaffolding). SERVING it is a SEPARATE, optional decision - see formula cell.

name: LTMLE - Longitudinal Effect
formula:
LTMLE - Longitudinal effect (doubly-robust; handles time-varying confounding):
Backward ICE (t=K..1):  Qbar_t^d = E[ Qbar_{t+1}^d | L_t, Abar_{t-1}=dbar ]
Targeting:  fluctuate Qbar_t with clever covariate  H_t = 1(Abar_t=dbar)/PROD_{s<=t} g_s ; solve EIC=0
Estimate:   psi_hat = (1/n) SUM_i Qbar_{1,i}^d   (dynamic-treatment effect)
MSM+IPTW alt:  w = PROD_t 1/g_t.  Keep DR-learner (G4) for single-time-point CATE.
[AIPW is the cross-sectional special case; LTMLE is the longitudinal upgrade.]

============ BUILD PATH  -  G5 = THE FULL UPGRADE (build SECOND) ============
WHY over G1-G4: LTMLE corrects TIME-VARYING confounding -> the correct answer to 'did FOLLOWING this
      regime over time actually help.' The static DR-learner (G4) cannot do this.
HOW to switch: THE INTERFACE IS IDENTICAL. Both G4 (tau_hat_DR) and G5 (psi_hat) output effect
      estimates to Layer H's benefit prior. So the upgrade is a DROP-IN SWAP at the H boundary -
      point H's benefit prior from tau_hat_DR to psi_hat. NO change to H's code, none to any other layer.
WHEN  switch once (1) the longitudinal outcome log is mature and (2) the regime + outcome definitions
      are clinically signed off. Until then: ship the G4 interim; keep LTMLE in shadow mode
      (compute + log, do not serve).
inputs: G2 nuisance (Qbar_t,g_t); user longitudinal history L_t,A_t,Y
outputs: psi_hat effect estimates -> Layer H benefit prior
units: FULL PATH - heavy offline, scoped (see handoff). Upgrade from G4 interim; swap at H's benefit prior, no H change. → see ★ Scoped Builds — LTMLE Bandit (this workbook) → ★ Uncertainty Memory E-F-G-H → ★ Clinical Calibration E-value

name: Conservative Safe Action Selection
formula:
STEP 1 - hard safety:
A_safe = {a: NOT Veto(a) AND Risk_UCB(a) <= risk_limit(a)}

STEP 2 - conservative ranking:
Benefit_LCB(a) = mu_b(a) - z_b*sigma_b(a)
Risk_UCB(a)    = mu_r(a) + z_r*sigma_r(a)
U_phys(a)      = trace(J_a * P_x * J_a^T)

Score(a) = Benefit_LCB(a)
         - lambda_r*Risk_UCB(a)
         - lambda_u*U_phys(a)
         - lambda_b*burden(a)
         + I_low_risk_behavior(a)*PolicyBonus(a)

a* = argmax_{a in A_safe} Score(a).
inputs: A_safe, benefit/risk distributions, P_x, J_a, burden, baseline policy
outputs: One safe action with lower-bound benefit and uncertainty audit

name: Safety Constraints
formula:
A_safe = {a in A : g_c(a) <= 0 for every active canonical rule c}

Load the complete active registry by canonical rule_id from MERGE·VETO Drug-Nutrient 339 (currently 339 unique rules, including 94 HARD_VETO rows). Named subsets may be used only when their scope is explicit and every subset ID resolves to the active registry.
+ Tolerable Upper Limits
+ drug/condition/action eligibility constraints
inputs:
Clinical rules
User medications
Medical history

name: Design Matrix Update
formula:
A_a  <-  A_a  +  phi(x,a) * phi(x,a)^T

Sherman-Morrison:  O(d^2) update
inputs: (x, a, r) experience tuple

name: Parameter Update
formula:
theta_hat_a  =  A_a^{-1} * b_a
b_a  <-  b_a  +  r * phi(x, a)
inputs: (x, a, r) experience tuple

name: Conservative Baseline Lagrangian
formula:
Conservative baseline guarantee + constraints:
Choose a only if the lower confidence bound of cumulative policy value satisfies

LCB[V_target(1:t)] >= (1-epsilon_base) * LCB[V_baseline(1:t)].

Then optimize:
L(a,lambda) = Score(a) - SUM_c lambda_c*g_c(a)

The baseline is the current evidence-based low-risk policy. If the guarantee or
off-policy-evaluation support fails, select the baseline action.
inputs: Baseline policy; constraints; lower confidence values
outputs: Constrained score and fail-closed baseline decision
units: scalar See handoff: LTMLE_Bandit build spec. → see ★ Scoped Builds — LTMLE Bandit (this workbook) → ★ Uncertainty Memory E-F-G-H → ★ Clinical Calibration E-value

name: Dual Variable Update
formula: lambda_c  <-  max(0,  lambda_c  +  eta * g_c(a*))
inputs: Constraint violations

name: Separated Uncertainty / Value of Information
formula:
Separate the two uncertainties:

PolicyBonus(a) = alpha * sqrt(phi(x,a)^T * A_a^-1 * phi(x,a))
  - epistemic uncertainty in the learned reward model;
  - enabled only for low-risk behavioral actions after offline evaluation.

Physiological uncertainty is conservative:
U_phys(a) = trace(J_a * P_x * J_a^T)
and enters Score with a NEGATIVE coefficient -lambda_u.

Information-gathering actions use a separate value-of-information score:
Score_info(a) = E[ KL(p(x|y,a) || p(x)) ] - lambda_b*burden(a).

Never use a supplement/physiological intervention merely to explore uncertainty.
inputs: Bandit parameter covariance A_a^-1; physiological covariance P_x; action Jacobian J_a
outputs: Policy bonus, physiological uncertainty penalty, or information-action score
units: reward units See handoff: LTMLE_Bandit build spec. → see ★ Scoped Builds — LTMLE Bandit (this workbook) → ★ Uncertainty Memory E-F-G-H

name: Directed Cluster Cascade
formula: E_k_coupled = E_k + eta_net * SUM_{j!=k} Gamma_jk * max(0, (E_j - theta_casc_j)/s_j)

correction_applied: RESEARCH_SHADOW; eta_net=0 in production. Stability uses the complete coupled Jacobian. If a Laplacian L=D-Gamma is ever used for diffusion, the sign is -eta*L*E.

formula: g_i(t)=SUM_k A_k(t)*cos(2*pi*k*t/1440 + phi_k(t));  m_i(t)=exp(g_i(t)) / mean_24h[exp(g_i)]
